knowledge:
- key_parameters: channels=specifies the fluorescence or scatter channels to use for gating or binning ;; preselection=a channel or population used to perform a rough preselection (e.g., back-gating) before fitting a norm2Filter ;; scale=scale factor for the gate size in lymphGate ;; sd=standard deviation multiplier to determine gate boundaries in quadrantGate and rangeGate ;; populations=the populations/nodes in the GatingSet to normalize ;; dims=the dimensions (channels) to normalize ;; minCountThreshold=minimum event count threshold for normalization ;; minRow=terminating condition for binning, typically a minimum number of events per bin (e.g., 5% of total events)
- alternatives: flowClust package can be used for mixture modeling to segment multiple sub-populations simultaneously, whereas lymphGate is preferred when targeting a single sub-population like T-cells. warpSet can be used directly on a flowSet instead of using normalize on a GatingSet.
- when_to_use: Use when analyzing flow cytometry data with technical variation (channel shifts) across samples that requires alignment/normalization before applying common gates. Also use when automated gating (1D range gates, quadrant gates, or lymphocyte gates) or multivariate probability binning comparison is needed.
- pitfalls: Applying a constant gate across samples without normalization will fail if there are unforeseen shifts in fluorescence intensities caused by technical variation. Missing peaks in some samples can make landmark classification in warpSet/normalize harder because it is not clear which cell population a peak represents.

workflows.name: automated_gating_and_normalization
workflows.intent: Perform automated gating and landmark-based normalization on a GatingSet of flow cytometry data.
input: ITN (flowSet or GatingSet containing flow cytometry samples with FSC, SSC, and fluorescence channels)
workflows.stages: 1. Load data and transform fluorescence channels using GatingSet and transformerList ;; 2. Identify T-cells using lymphGate and add to the GatingSet ;; 3. Estimate quadrant gates using quadrantGate ;; 4. Normalize CD4 and CD8 channels across samples using normalize ;; 5. Identify activated T-helper cells using rangeGate and normalize the CD69 channel
workflows.code:
library(flowCore)
library(flowStats)
library(flowWorkspace)
library(ggcyto)
data(ITN)
require(scales)
gs <- GatingSet(ITN)
trans.func <- asinh
inv.func <- sinh
trans.obj <- trans_new("myAsinh", trans.func, inv.func)
transList <- transformerList(colnames(ITN)[3:7], trans.obj)
gs <- transform(gs, transList)
lg <- lymphGate(gs_cyto_data(gs), channels=c("CD3", "SSC"),
                preselection="CD4", filterId="TCells",
                scale=2.5)
gs_pop_add(gs, lg)
recompute(gs)
qgate <- quadrantGate(gs_pop_get_data(gs, "TCells"), stains=c("CD4", "CD8"),
                      filterId="CD4CD8", sd=3)
gs_pop_add(gs, qgate, parent = "TCells")
recompute(gs)
gs <- normalize(gs, populations=c("CD4+CD8+", "CD4+CD8-", "CD4-CD8+", "CD4-CD8-"), 
                     dims=c("CD4", "CD8"), minCountThreshold = 50)
CD69rg <- rangeGate(gs_cyto_data(gs), stain="CD69",
                    alpha=0.75, filterId="CD4+CD8-CD69", sd=2.5)
gs_pop_add(gs, CD69rg, parent="CD4+CD8-")
recompute(gs)
gs <- normalize(gs, populations=c("CD4+CD8-CD69"), 
                     dims=c("CD69"), minCountThreshold = 50)

workflows.name: probability_binning_comparison
workflows.intent: Quantitate multivariate distribution differences between experimental flow cytometry samples and a control sample using probability binning.
input: gs (GatingSet or flowSet containing normalized flow cytometry samples)
workflows.stages: 1. Extract flow data from GatingSet ;; 2. Create a control dataset by combining and subsampling flowFrames ;; 3. Apply probability binning to the control data using proBin ;; 4. Apply control bin positions to sample data using binByRef via fsApply ;; 5. Calculate Pearson Chi-Square and Roederer's probability binning statistics using calcPearsonChi and calcPBChiSquare
